title: Outer-stage condition on the reachable set
statement: Let $K$ and $L$ be natural numbers, let $R$ be a binary relation on the natural numbers, and let $	ext{Init}$ and $	ext{Acc}$ be predicates on the natural numbers. Suppose $B(t)$ holds exactly when $t$ is not reachable within $L$ steps from an initial number, for every $t<K$. The recursive condition over $K$ stages, starting at position $0$ with counter $0$, holds—requiring at each selected position that it be reachable and fail $	ext{Acc}$, using $B$ at the alternative positions, and ending with $	ext{Kont}$—if and only if every element of the reachable set fails $	ext{Acc}$ and $	ext{Kont}$ holds at the cardinality of that set.
hypotheses_covered: A binary relation R on natural numbers
Predicates Init and Acc on natural numbers
Predicates B and Kont on natural numbers
For every t < K, B(t) iff t is not reachable within L steps from an initial number
